skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Inspect the repository and applicable context, resolve assumptions, consider alternatives and critique your proposed solution before finalizing it. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For a scoped finding recovery Round, focus the plan on the requested correction against the retained candidate. Do not change repository files. Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

The bundled xterm consumed an OSC 52 probe without a browser clipboard write; Refine registers no OSC handler. This establishes a capability gap, not the reported session's cause. Claude documents mouse-owned selections and different local/remote clipboard paths: [Claude fullscreen documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen).

Native clipboard events and asynchronous clipboard APIs have different browser requirements: [MDN Clipboard API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard_API). xterm exposes a native-selection override for mouse-reporting mode: [xterm terminal options](https://xtermjs.org/docs/api/terminal/interfaces/iterminaloptions/).

checklist.description: Add tests using the shipped xterm renderer in tests/web_terminal_clipboard_browser.test.js, following the isolated static-server/API-fixture pattern in tests/web_screen_render.test.js. Reproduce keyboard and context-menu clipboard behavior with asynchronous clipboard access allowed, denied, and unavailable; also exercise alternate-screen and mouse-reporting modes. Record whether the failure concerns browser events, terminal selection, or application-generated clipboard output. Use an isolated Claude session for the provider smoke check and record its actual clipboard path.

Extract clipboard handling from the 3,087-line toolbar.js into a cohesive features/terminal-clipboard.js module with explicit renderer/session callbacks. Load it before toolbar.js in index.html and update affected test loaders. Make native browser copy/paste events authoritative for browser clipboard shortcuts: prevent xterm from interpreting those keystrokes without cancelling the browser action. Preserve supported terminal-specific shortcuts through a separate fallback with visible errors. Verify that one gesture produces one clipboard operation.

Provide reliable browser-owned selection while an agent captures the mouse: retain Shift-drag on Windows/Linux, enable xterm's macOptionClickForcesSelection for Option-drag on macOS, and expose a concise selection hint in the shared terminal surface. Preserve ordinary TUI mouse interaction. Copy the selected text without sending an interrupt; retain Ctrl+C terminal semantics when no xterm selection exists. Verify selection and clipboard contents with actual browser gestures.

Keep accepted paste text on Terminal.paste → onData → the existing managed-session input queue. Preserve line-ending normalization, application-controlled bracketed-paste framing, duplicate-event suppression, and replacement-session fencing. If P1 demonstrates that application-owned copying requires OSC 52, add a bounded, write-only handler in the clipboard module: validate payloads, respect browser permissions, restrict side effects to the current focused live session, and suppress transcript/history replay. Verify split sequences, malformed payloads, stale sessions, and denied writes before accepting that extension.

Extend focused regressions across Terminal, Agent, Planning Agent, Goal, Standalone/Agent in Worktree, and Skill profiles, with Claude and another provider represented. Cover Unicode and multiline paste, bracketed mode enabled/disabled, no duplicate input, tab changes, session replacement, retained renderer remounts, and focus outside the terminal. Preserve Ctrl+Enter, Agent Ctrl+Z suppression, shell job control, and command-palette precedence. Move reusable clipboard test scaffolding into tests/support if needed to keep files cohesive.

Update only docs/intent/05-surfaces/03-browser/19-terminal.md to describe the provider-independent text clipboard contract, selection gestures, and browser restrictions; document OSC behavior only if implemented. From the pinned worktree run node --test tests/web_terminal_clipboard.test.js tests/web_terminal_clipboard_browser.test.js tests/web_supervisor_toolbar.test.js tests/web_command_palette.test.js tests/web_javascript_syntax.test.js, plus git diff --check. Require executed browser tests and a Claude copy/paste smoke check for completion; report missing tooling and skips explicitly. Keep source promotion, serving-daemon restart, Goal transitions, merge, and push outside this Round.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: Passing mock tests do not establish the cause of the reported Claude failure. P1 requires real xterm/browser reproduction and an observed provider clipboard path before attributing the failure or adding protocol support.

A Claude-specific mouse-disable setting or unconditional OSC 52 bridge would weaken native interaction or introduce replay side effects. The primary correction uses shared browser clipboard events and native selection; protocol support has an explicit evidence gate and session/replay constraints.

Adding more responsibilities to toolbar.js would worsen its structure. Extract only the clipboard responsibility and associated tests, preserving the existing Application/Infrastructure input path, managed-session lifecycle, geometry, and shortcut contracts.
